summary.headline: One central control plane — not three — should govern every AI agent: here is the identity, audit, governance, and guardrail blueprint to build.
summary.narrative: Synthesized from the Customer Success and Sales deployment-guardrails packs. The Marketing guardrails pack (mkt-deployment-guardrails) was not present in readiness-output, so the data-governance and catalog elements below cover CS and Sales only — re-run this blueprint once the Marketing pack exists to close that gap. The blueprint reconciles the packs into one least-privilege identity model, one unified audit trail, one PII/retention governance policy, and one central guardrail catalog. This is a blueprint a human implements; this tool deploys nothing.

findings.title: Least-privilege identity model: one scoped service identity per agent, no shared credential
findings.what_we_found: The CS pack requests read/write on Cases and Knowledge; the Sales pack requests read/write on Opportunities and Contacts. Neither specifies a distinct service identity — both assume a broad operator credential, and their scopes overlap on Contacts inconsistently.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: A shared or over-broad credential means a compromised or mis-prompted agent can act far beyond its job, and you cannot attribute an action to a specific agent. There is no least-privilege boundary for an AI to operate safely behind.
the_fix: Define one service identity per agent (cs-agent, sales-agent), each scoped to the minimum objects/fields/actions that team's AI needs.
Separate read scopes from write scopes; grant write only where the pack justifies it.
Require human-in-the-loop confirmation for every write or send action; the agent proposes, a human commits.
Eliminate any shared 'god' credential; reconcile the overlapping Contacts scope to the narrower of the two requests.
findings.evidence: Both packs request write access; neither defines a per-agent identity; Contacts scope differs between packs.

findings.title: Unified audit-trail spec: one append-only log every agent writes to
findings.what_we_found: The CS and Sales packs describe logging differently — one logs actions, the other logs only errors — and neither captures the grounding/inputs behind an action.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Without one consistent, complete audit trail you cannot reconstruct why an agent did what it did, prove compliance, or investigate an incident across teams.
the_fix: Adopt one append-only audit schema: acting identity, action, target record, inputs/grounding used, timestamp, and outcome.
Require every agent action (read-into-context and write) to emit a record before the action is considered complete.
Store the log immutably with a defined retention window and restrict who can read it.
Reconcile both packs' logging to this single spec.
findings.evidence: Inconsistent logging between packs; no grounding/inputs captured in either.

findings.title: Context & data governance: PII handling, retention, and privacy floor
findings.what_we_found: The CS pack touches case content that can contain customer PII; the Sales pack reads contact records. Neither specifies a redaction rule, a retention window for context data, or a privacy stance — and the Marketing pack (which would carry the consent/PII rules) is missing.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: An agent that reads PII into context with no retention or redaction rule creates uncontrolled copies of sensitive data and an unclear privacy posture — a real exposure before any model even responds.
the_fix: Define what counts as PII/sensitive across teams and redact or mask it before it enters agent context where not required.
Set a retention window for context/transient data and enforce deletion at expiry.
Adopt the strictest stance across the packs as the floor for all agents.
Re-run this blueprint once mkt-deployment-guardrails exists so marketing consent/PII rules are folded in.
Validate the retention and privacy choices with counsel before go-live.
findings.evidence: PII-bearing case/contact data in scope; no redaction or retention rule in either present pack; marketing pack absent.

findings.title: Central guardrail catalog: one reconciled list of every guardrail any agent must honor
findings.what_we_found: The CS and Sales packs each list guardrails (scope limits, escalation triggers, prohibited actions); some overlap, some conflict (different thresholds for human escalation).
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Three separate guardrail lists mean no single source of truth — a guardrail tightened for one team silently doesn't apply to another, and conflicts go unresolved.
the_fix: Merge the packs' guardrails into one catalog, de-duplicating identical rules.
Resolve every conflict to the stricter rule and record the decision.
Make the catalog the single reference every agent's configuration is validated against by a human.
Flag the marketing pack's guardrails as a known gap until that pack is produced.
findings.evidence: Overlapping guardrails with conflicting escalation thresholds between the two packs.
